shown.message:
The smallest-κ results from `analysis` (`experiment-repo`#12) are in. They overturn part of what I said last turn, and they are recorded in Brief rev. 23.

**What the new rows show:**
- **Block, smooth mechanisms (423 cells):**
  - The true-M interval reaches 0.90 at about the oracle's width: 0.913 at 1.04×. A uniform inflation of the same width gives 0.900.
  - The cubic B₂ needs 9.6× the oracle width on the same cells.
  - So on these cells the width price of B₂ is the M̂ noise. The right curvature class costs little, but adds almost nothing over plain width.
- **Original cells, smooth pool:** the true-M interval never reaches 0.90 (0.895), so the block reading does not replicate. I read the arm as mixed across the two sources, leaning to the cubic M̂ on the block, and I do not claim the price is only M̂ noise.
- **(b) and (e):** the true-M interval stays at 0.59 at any κ, because the bias is the wrong exposure variable, not curvature in f. The cubic B₂ gets 0.966 there only at 6.7× the oracle width, through noise.
- **Lean arm:** it never reaches 0.90 in any pool, because subtracting the null column removes signal along with noise. I dropped it as a stand-in for the truth.

My rev. 22 line "some price remains with the true M (0.942 at 2.2×)" was read at κ = 1, below the coverage target, so rev. 23 replaces it. The claim that survives is that the cost of honest coverage depends on the class of assumption more than on non-identification as such. With the right class and bound it is cheap on smooth responses. With the wrong class, no width of that class helps. With the bound estimated from the data, the width is noise. The paper states no price for non-identification.

`paper-repo` had already applied the κ* rows to its text, and I added a note on the lean arm and (b)/(e). I opened `story-repo`#9 so the Outline replaces the "2.2×" wording, and I closed `experiment-repo`#12. I'm waiting on `story-repo` for #9, and I'll respond to any further review of rev. 23.
